data.text:
Handoff from the planning session (2026-09-14). Read in this order before touching code:

1. project/2026-09-14-architecture-plan.md — Decisions and Invariants are binding; each leaf names its files.
2. project/2026-09-14-research-findings.md — the verified wire facts. Sections 1 (Anthropic), 2 (OpenRouter) and 3 (Go 1.27) are what the provider and foundation leaves implement; do not re-research them, and do not trust prior training on json/v2 tag names (`embed`, not `inline`; no `format` or `unknown` options).
3. project/gotchas.md and project/backlog.md.

Things that are true but easy to get wrong:

- Go builds and git both fail inside the Bash sandbox ("package fmt is not in std", unreadable ~/.gitconfig); re-run that one call with the sandbox off. File edits and `job` work sandboxed.
- json/v2 marshaler funcs may receive *T rather than T for union members; handle both.
- Property order in tool schemas is load-bearing: never a map anywhere a schema lives.
- On OpenRouter the trailing usage frame repeats finish_reason; on both providers a 200 can carry an error body.
- Thinking blocks are opaque: keep the provider's raw block and re-emit it byte-exact and in order. Never edit an earlier turn.
- The `claude-api` skill will tell you to use anthropic-sdk-go; the core takes no dependencies. Use the skill for facts only.
- API keys will be in .env (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY) when the fixture leaves are reached; the unit suite must pass without them.

Suggested first moves: `job orient` points at the scaffold leaf (fzGDQ2). The foundation leaves after it (blocks, schema, vocab, sse, markdown) are disjoint by file and can fan out to parallel agents once the scaffold lands; tools and stream depend on them. Both providers can then run in parallel. Verification scratch from planning (a json/v2 and generic-method probe) is disposable and lives only in the session scratchpad.

data.note: Landed in 40266fd. LICENSE was already committed by the planning session. deps_test.go reads the root and internal/sse with go/build (Imports, TestImports, XTestImports); std detection is the go tool's rule (no dot in the first path element, "C" excluded). External test packages may import subpackages so end-to-end tests can reach the providers. A package directory that does not exist yet is logged and skipped, not failed, so the guard could land first. Mutation proof: a root file importing a throwaway internal/mut package failed on the test's own assertion; a root file importing github.com/example/dep failed at test setup. gofmt, go vet, go fix and go mod tidy clean.

data.text: Carve (2026-09-14, integrator): request.go leaves this leaf and goes to the stream leaf (wuxgDE), because Request references Message (blocks leaf) and Tool (tools leaf) and would not compile in this wave. cache.go (CachePolicy, CacheTTL, CacheControl) was written on main in c6ab86a ahead of the fan-out because the block model needs the marker type; do not rewrite it. Budget lives in the loop leaf (n1qE9c, budget.go). This leaf's files are now: thinking.go, usage.go, capabilities.go, errors.go and tests. Enums are string-typed so an unknown wire value survives decoding; the zero value of Effort is Default and of CachePolicy is Auto.

Carve (2026-09-14, integrator): this leaf also owns request.go (the Request struct, with System as []Text so a cache marker can sit on a system block, and Extensions) and provider.go (Provider, Completer, ModelLister). It now depends on tools (5NAbHV) as well, for Request.Tools []Tool.
Carve (2026-09-14, integrator): Budget (MaxTurns default 20, MaxTokens, Timeout) belongs here in budget.go, not in the vocabulary leaf.

Carve (2026-09-14, integrator): CacheControl already exists in cache.go (c6ab86a); blocks that can carry a breakpoint hold `Cache *CacheControl` with json tag "cache,omitzero". Roles are User, Assistant and System (System for mid-conversation system messages, which both providers accept). Tool results are blocks inside a user message, as on Anthropic; OpenRouter translates them to role tool messages.

Implemented internal/sse (sse.go, sse_test.go, split_test.go) per the architecture plan's SSE leaf and the WHATWG event-stream spec.

TDD: wrote sse_test.go and split_test.go first, referencing Event/Events/eventsWithLimit/splitSSELines before any implementation existed; `go test ./internal/sse/...` failed to compile (undefined: Event, Events, splitSSELines, ...) confirming red. One gotcha hit while writing tests: a Go string literal containing an actual BOM character (`"﻿"`) makes the compiler reject the *source file itself* with "illegal byte order mark" — Go disallows a literal BOM anywhere in source except as the very first bytes. Fixed by using the byte escape `"\xEF\xBB\xBF"` instead, which is plain ASCII in the source and only becomes the BOM bytes at runtime. Documented this in project/gotchas.md.

Design:
- Event{Type, Data, ID, Retry} as decided. Events(io.Reader) iter.Seq2[Event, error]: a pure pull iterator, no goroutine, so an early `break` by the consumer just stops calling Read — proved with a byte-counting reader.
- Custom bufio.SplitFunc (splitSSELines) handles LF/CRLF/lone-CR, including a CR at the very end of a buffered chunk (asks bufio.Scanner for more data unless atEOF, so a CRLF pair split across reads is never mis-split — proved with iotest.OneByteReader end-to-end and with direct two-call unit tests).
- BOM stripped via bufio.Reader.Peek(3)/Discard before the Scanner is attached.
- Buffer capped at 64 MiB via scanner.Buffer(initial, max), with initial = min(4096, max) so a test can inject a tiny max (64 bytes) and prove an oversized line yields bufio.ErrTooLong rather than being silently dropped, without allocating a real 64 MiB line in the test.
- Two decided deviations from the literal WHATWG algorithm, both documented on Events' doc comment:
  1. (given in the brief) event: arriving while data is pending dispatches the pending event first, as if a blank line preceded it.
  2. (my own consistent extension, not explicit in the brief) ID and Retry do NOT carry forward across dispatches the way the spec's "last event id buffer" does — every Event reflects only the fields its own group set. The brief explicitly decided this for ID ("keep the API simple: ID is what this event set") but was silent on Retry; I applied the same rule to Retry for consistency, since the alternative (Retry persisting silently across events, ID not) would be an inconsistent, surprising API. Flagging this explicitly since it's an extrapolation, not a literal instruction.
- Event.Type defaults to "message" when no event: field was ever sent for that dispatch, per spec (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/server-sent-events.html#dispatchMessage). The brief's DECIDED API section didn't state this default explicitly; implemented it because omitting it would make every default-typed OpenRouter/Anthropic-shaped test data line come back with Type == "", which no consumer would want.

Verified before handback (worktree, sandbox disabled): go fix ./..., gofmt -l . (empty), go vet ./..., go mod tidy (no-op, confirms zero deps), go build ./..., go test -race ./... — all green, whole module. internal/sse/sse.go is 237 lines, sse_test.go 286, split_test.go 73 — all comfortably under the 400-line ceiling.

data.text:
Vocabulary landed on wt/vocab (worktree .claude/worktrees/vocab), not committed.

Files: stop_reason.go, thinking.go, usage.go, decimal.go, capabilities.go, errors.go plus a test file for each. `go fix ./...`, `gofmt -l .`, `go vet ./...` clean; `go test -race ./...` passes (38 tests, all red first).

Three judgement calls the next reader should know:

1. **Decimal is a canonical decimal string, not a *big.Int + scale.** Arithmetic converts to math/big on demand and canonicalises the result ("" is zero, no exponent, no trailing zeros), so two Decimals holding the same number are always `==`. A `*big.Int` field would have made `Cost == Cost` and `Pricing == Pricing` compare pointers silently, and a `big.Int` value field would have made those structs uncomparable and unsafe to copy. Prices are parsed once and added a few thousand times per run, so re-parsing per op costs nothing that matters. Untrusted input is bounded: at most 4096 significant digits and |scale| <= 4096, so "1e2000000000" is an error rather than a 2 GB allocation.

2. **Cost.Add treats the zero Cost as the identity, then ANDs Reported.** Strict AND alone makes the natural accumulator (`var total Cost; total = total.Add(c)`) report false forever, because the empty accumulator is unreported. Anthropic's "no cost reported" *is* the zero Cost, so it contributes nothing and clears nothing; a non-identity leg that was not reported still poisons the total, because a sum that omits a leg must not present itself as a provider's figure. Costs in different currencies are summed but marked not reported.

3. **StopReason gained `StopNone = ""`** (the brief listed only the six wire values) so the zero value has a name and `Known()` can be true for every constant the package defines. `Known()` is therefore an "is this one of ours" check, not an "is this set" check; ask `== StopNone` for the latter.

Also worth knowing downstream: `Capabilities` carries `ThinkingEfforts []Effort`, so `Capabilities` and `ModelInfo` are not comparable with `==` — tests compare field by field. `ErrorKind("")` normalises to `KindUnknown` in String, Retryable and `(*APIError).Is`, so an unmapped error still answers `errors.Is(err, KindUnknown)`.

Cost distinguishes reported from not reported

data.text: Vocabulary implemented and verified on wt/vocab; handing back to the integrator to commit and close.

Block model implemented: block.go, source.go, block_json.go, message.go, conversation.go and four test files. Suite green: `go test -race ./...` in the wt/blocks worktree; `go fix`, `gofmt -l`, `go vet`, `go mod tidy` all clean.

## json/v2 facts verified on go1.27.0 (scratch probe, then the suite)

1. **A bare `[]Block` cannot be unmarshalled.** `json.Unmarshal(data, &[]Block{})` fails with "cannot derive concrete type for nil interface with finite type set": json/v2 needs an `UnmarshalFromFunc` option for a non-empty interface, and a plain slice type gives nowhere to attach one. So a block list is the named type `Blocks []Block`, whose `UnmarshalJSONFrom` installs the dispatch internally. `Message.Content` and `ToolResult.Content` are `Blocks`; since `Blocks` and `[]Block` are mutually assignable, callers write `UserMessage(Text{...})` and `[]Block` parameters accept it unchanged. Plain `json.Marshal`/`Unmarshal` on a Message, a Conversation, and on `Blocks`, all round-trip with no options. The plan is corrected in place.

2. **Marshalling needs no options at all.** Each block type carries a `MarshalJSONTo` that writes its own `"type"` tag first, so a block is self-describing wherever it appears rather than only inside a container that knows to tag it. The tag is spliced on by a generic `tagged[T]{Type; Body T json:",embed"}` over a method-less defined type (`type textBody Text`), which keeps one struct per concept — the body types share the real struct's fields and tags, they are not hand-written twins. `,embed` (json/v2's rename of `inline`) works on a generic field.

3. **`[]byte` encodes as base64 by default.** No option needed for `Source.Data`.

4. **A `jsontext.Value` does not survive arbitrary whitespace.** The encoder reformats on `WriteValue`: insignificant whitespace is stripped and string escapes are normalised (`é` becomes the literal, `\/` becomes `/`); `jsontext.PreserveRawStrings` does not change this on the marshal path. What *is* preserved: member order, every member, and numbers verbatim. Provider wire bytes are compact, so `Thinking.Raw` and `Unknown.Raw` are byte-identical in practice, and semantically identical always. `TestThinkingRawSurvivesNesting` pins member-order preservation with a deliberately out-of-order raw block.

5. **`Decoder.ReadValue` bytes must be cloned.** Verified by mutation: with the `bytes.Clone` removed, decoding 40 blocks through `json.UnmarshalRead` over a `iotest.OneByteReader` gives block 0 a `Raw` of `,#"type":"alpha2"...` — the decoder had refilled its buffer underneath. Decoding the same input from a `[]byte` shows nothing, because that path aliases the caller's slice. Any future code that keeps bytes from a decoder (the SSE/stream leaf will) needs the same clone, and needs a reader-based test to catch its absence.

## Design decisions

- **Unknown is the fallback for a missing or unrecognised type tag** (invariant 6: surface, never drop), and it re-marshals as its raw bytes, so a block goodall does not understand passes through storage and back to the provider. A *known* type whose body is malformed is a decode error naming the block type instead — the two failures are different and stay distinguishable.
- **`Conversation.Append` allocates an exact-capacity slice.** The test asserts `cap == len` after every append as well as forking twice from the same value at eight different lengths; the behavioural fork check alone is not enough, because a naive `append` only aliases once the growth policy has left headroom (it first bites at length 3).
- **Accessors deep-copy far enough to matter**: the message's `Content` slice and any nested `ToolResult.Content`. `jsontext.Value` bytes are shared, read-only — nothing in the library writes through them, and copying every raw thinking block on every `At` would be the expensive part of a long thread.
- `is_error` and `partial` are `omitzero`, so a plain result and a complete turn carry no noise. `ToolUse.Input` is `omitzero` too, which keeps a nil input round-tripping as nil rather than as the four bytes `null`.
- `Conversation{}` marshals as `[]` rather than `null`, so a persisted thread always has one shape.

## Deviations from the brief

- `Blocks` named type, and `Message.Content`/`ToolResult.Content` typed as it (finding 1 — the brief's shape cannot decode).
- Marshalling by method rather than by `MarshalToFunc` (finding 2; the brief left the mechanism to the implementer).
- `Unknown.Type` is `BlockType`, a string enum, not `string`; `BlockType` constants name the seven known tags.
- Added `SystemMessage`, since `RoleSystem` exists and the other two roles have constructors.

## Gaps for whoever picks this up

- Nothing here validates a block's contents — an `Image` with no source, a `ToolResult` whose content holds a `ToolUse`. That belongs with the request builder, which knows what a provider accepts.
- `Blocks` is the only decode entry point. If an event or thread type outside this package needs a bare `[]Block` field, it wants `Blocks` instead, or this package should export the unmarshalers.

data.text:
Schema type and inference landed in wt/schema (schema.go, schema_infer.go, schema_test.go, schema_infer_test.go). `go fix`, `gofmt -l`, `go vet`, `go test -race ./...` all clean.

Shape as built:
- `Schema` is a plain struct whose eight members emit in a fixed order (type, description, enum, properties, required, additionalProperties, items, format), unset ones omitted by `omitzero`. `json.Marshal` with no options produces provider-ready bytes.
- `Properties []Property` carries its own MarshalJSONTo/UnmarshalJSONFrom so it is a JSON object on the wire but an ordered slice in Go. `Property.Schema` is a **value**, not a pointer (the brief left the choice open) — it removes a whole class of nil checks from Validate.
- `AdditionalProperties` is a named string with Unset/Forbidden/Allowed and a bool on the wire, so "absent" and "false" are different values rather than one zero bool.
- A nil `Properties` emits no `properties` member; an **empty non-nil** one emits `"properties":{}`. Inference always produces the non-nil form, so a no-parameter tool gets the `{"type":"object","properties":{}}` shape Anthropic documents.
- Errors are a typed `*SchemaError{Path, Reason}` so the tools leaf can report the field path without scraping the message.

Inference was written against **measured** json/v2 behaviour, not the assumed rules; the verified facts are now recorded as a dated block quote in project/2026-09-14-research-findings.md §3. The four that changed the implementation:

1. `[N]byte` is base64 like `[]byte` (and refuses a JSON array on the way back), while a slice of a *named* byte type stays a JSON array. The test is "element type is exactly `byte`".
2. An embedded field of **unexported type** is still encoded by json/v2, both flattened and when given an explicit JSON name. A first cut skipped it on `IsExported()` and silently dropped the property.
3. The `,string` tag option makes a number a JSON **string** and json/v2 then rejects a bare number, so such a field must infer as `string`; on a bool or string field json/v2 errors, and so does inference.
4. `encoding.TextMarshaler` beats structural encoding (`netip.Addr`, `time.Time`), and `time.Duration` has *no* representation in json/v2 at all — a schema promising an integer there would produce input the handler could never decode, so it is an inference error.

Embedded flattening implements json/v2's real depth rule: depth-first in place, a shallower field shadows a deeper one of the same name and keeps its own position, and two fields at the same depth claiming one name is an error. Recursion detection is path-scoped, so a struct used twice on sibling branches is fine while a type that reaches itself is an error naming the path.

For the tools leaf: call `SchemaFor[In]()` then `(*Schema).Validate()`. Validate does the five structural checks plus "additionalProperties only on an object", and recurses into properties and items with a dotted path (`origin.x`, `tags[]`) in the message.

Two things deliberately NOT done, for the owner to rule on:
- `[]byte` infers as a bare `{"type":"string"}` with no hint that the value must be base64. Adding `"format":"byte"` (OpenAPI's convention, widely recognised by models) would cut a likely decode failure; the brief only specified a format for `time.Time`, so it was left alone.
- `Validate` does not require an array schema to carry `items`. Inference always supplies one, but a hand-built `{"type":"array"}` meaning "any array" is legal JSON Schema and is allowed through.

Two findings worth carrying forward.

1. Stack overflow, fixed. Block-quote parsing recursed once per ">" on a line;
   2 MiB of them exhausted the 1 GB goroutine stack — a fatal error Go cannot

   backtick run / emphasis run / "]" / ")" remains). Proved by mutation: with
   the memos removed the 4 MiB TestLargeInputFinishes input took 28.8s; with
   them, 44ms (go test ./chat/markdown -run TestLargeInputFinishes -v). The test

internal/transport built on wt/transport (worktree .claude/worktrees/transport). Four source files: transport.go (Client, Request, Do, build, errorFor, KindForStatus), retry.go (defaults, full-jitter backoff, ctx-aware wait, Retry-After and request-id header parsing), body.go (the ctx-bound response body), plus fakes_test.go / transport_test.go / retry_test.go / stream_test.go. `go test -race ./...` passes; `go fix`, `gofmt -l`, `go vet`, `go mod tidy` clean.

Shape as decided in the integrator note, with these findings worth carrying into the provider tasks:

1. `MaxRetries` cannot express "no retries" with a zero field, because zero is what an uninitialised struct carries and zero means "take the default of 2". A negative value is the opt-out, and the field doc says so. The alternative (a *int) was not worth the pointer.

2. The cancellation promise needed a watcher goroutine, not just a read guard. net/http closes the body on ctx cancel only because the real Transport tears the connection down; an injected RoundTripper (a recorder, a replayer, a test fake) has no connection, so "cancelling ctx closes the body" would have been a promise that held only over real sockets. `newContextBody` therefore parks one goroutine per streamed response on `select { ctx.Done(); stop }`, released by Close (idempotent via sync.Once). It is skipped entirely when ctx.Done() is nil — a context that can never be cancelled needs no watcher, and a goroutine parked on a nil channel is NOT durably blocked, which would stall a synctest bubble.

3. synctest note for whoever writes the provider stream tests: inside a bubble, derive contexts from context.Background() rather than from t.Context(). The bubble's root goroutine exit waits for every bubbled goroutine, so a watcher parked on a context that is only cancelled when the test function returns is a deadlock. `context.WithCancel(context.Background())` inside the bubble creates a Done channel that is unambiguously bubbled, and `defer cancel()` releases the watcher.

4. Retry-After and the delay interact in three ways, all tested: honoured exactly and jitter-free when present and within MaxRetryAfter (default 30s); the error returned unretried, with RetryAfter set, when it is longer than that (the caller decides whether to sleep 15 minutes); and ignored when it is zero, negative, unparseable or an HTTP-date already in the past, which falls back to jitter rather than to a number nobody sent.

5. KindForStatus returns KindUnknown for anything it cannot place, including a status below 400 — the brief's table only covered >= 400, and a 3xx that escapes the redirect follower should not be classified by guesswork.

6. The fallback Message is truncated at 1024 bytes (the body is read bounded at 1 MiB). The full body still travels on Raw when it is valid JSON, so nothing is lost and an error stays printable in a log line.

Mutation proofs run rather than asserted: dropping the watcher goroutine fails TestCancelMidBodyClosesBody, TestDoCancelMidBodyOverRealConnection and TestDoReturnsSuccessBodyOpen; ignoring Retry-After when choosing the delay fails the two Retry-After timing tests, TestRetryAfterAboveCapIsNotRetried and TestDoRetriesOverRealConnection; dropping the truncation fails TestDoFallbackTruncatesAHugeBody.

Nothing outside internal/transport was touched. deps_test.go's stdOnly list is unchanged and should stay that way: internal/transport imports the root package by design, so it does not belong in a std-only list.

Built NewTool[In], typedTool, the schema-aware decode-error message and the ToolResult helpers on branch wt/tools. Files: tool.go (extended), tool_error.go (new, the message text), tool_result.go (new), tool_test.go, tool_error_test.go, tool_result_test.go. go fix / gofmt -l / go vet / go mod tidy / go test -race all clean.

DECISION — required parameters. Verified on go1.27.0 darwin/arm64 (scratch module, json.Unmarshal with RejectUnknownMembers): encoding/json/v2 does NOT enforce required members. `{}` decodes into a struct with no error, leaving every field at its zero value, so a model that omits `city` would silently run the tool on "". That breaks the promise the schema made to the model, so Execute checks the decoded object against the schema's Required list after a successful decode — recursively, through nested objects (`window.start`) and array elements (`points[1].lon`) — and returns the same IsError shape a decode failure returns: `missing required parameter "window.start"` (plural: `missing required parameters "query" and "window"`). An author happy with the zero value marks the field omitzero, which is exactly what makes it optional in the schema. Cost: one extra pass over the input as map[string]jsontext.Value per call. Recorded as a block quote under the plan's Tools paragraph.

DECISION — the error text. One problem line, a blank line, then the whole parameter listing in schema order:

    parameter "days" takes an integer, but the value sent was 3.5

    Parameters:
      city (string, required): the city to look up
      units (string, optional, one of "celsius", "fahrenheit"): temperature units
      days (integer, optional): how many days to forecast

Nested objects get dotted names, array elements a [] suffix (`points[].lat`), arrays their element type (`array of string`), time.Time-style fields their format. A tool with no parameters says "This tool takes no parameters." rather than an empty heading. Problem lines: `unknown parameter "window.stop"`, `parameter "x" takes …, but the value sent was …`, `the input must be a JSON object, but …`, `the input is not valid JSON: <jsontext inner error>`, `missing required parameter(s) …`.

FACT worth knowing downstream: json/v2 populates SemanticError.JSONValue only when it rejected a string's or number's *content* (3.5 into an int); a plain kind mismatch (string into int) carries JSONKind only. So the message names the literal when it has one and the JSON kind otherwise — it cannot always echo the value.

Also: an absent input (nil, empty, whitespace, `null`) is read as `{}`; `Schema()` returns the same *Schema pointer every call; result helpers leave ToolUseID empty; run's result and error pass through untouched; run is not called at all when the input fails to decode.

New exported identifier beyond the brief: `MaxToolNameLength = 64` (both providers' limit), so a consumer can validate a name before constructing a tool.

Mutation check done: reversing the property iteration in appendParameterLines made both listing-order assertions fail with the reversed text, then reverted.

Built on wt/stream: request.go, provider.go, result.go, event.go, event_json.go, accumulate.go, stream.go and four test files. `go fix ./...`, `gofmt -l .` (clean), `go vet ./...`, `go mod tidy`, `go test -race ./...` all pass in the worktree.

Decisions the next leaves need:

1. **`UnknownEvent`, not `Unknown`.** The brief's event name collided with the `Unknown` *block* in the same package. It is `UnknownEvent{EventType EventType; Raw jsontext.Value}`, tagged `{"type":"unknown","event_type":"<provider tag>","raw":{...}}`. Unlike the unknown block it does NOT re-emit raw verbatim: an event goes to a front end and never back to a provider, so a front end's switch on `type` never meets a surprise value.

2. **`Event` has an exported `Type() EventType`** alongside the unexported seal, so the chat layer can route or log without a full type switch, and `EventType.FromLoop()` splits the loop's six from the provider's ten.

3. **Usage folding: later report wins field by field, zero means "not reported here".** Anthropic puts the input side on `message_start` and cumulative counts on `message_delta`; OpenRouter sends one trailing frame. Counts only grow within a message, so a zero in the later report is silence, not a reset, and the earlier figure stands. `laterUsage` in accumulate.go; three table cases in TestAccumulatorUsage.

4. **`Accumulator.Response()` is never nil**, at any point in the stream; `Message.Partial` is the single signal of completeness. `Collect` therefore always hands back a response, even alongside an error, so a cancelled stream still yields its text and its usage.

5. **An open tool call's `Input` is left empty in `Message()`/`snapshot()`.** Half a JSON document is not a JSON value and a `Message` holding one fails to marshal exactly when a UI wants to draw it. The fragments are on the `ToolInputDelta` events for anyone who wants them; at `BlockStop` an empty input becomes `{}` and an invalid one is a `*ProtocolError` (a truncated call must never run).

6. **`Prefix()` stops at the first still-open block** rather than returning every finished block, because a prefix is what can be replayed and a thinking signature binds everything after it.

7. **`ProtocolError` lives in stream.go** (with `Stream`, `Collect`, `CollectResult`), not accumulate.go, which was over the 400-line ceiling with it.

8. Providers: `ToolChoice.Validate()` is there to be called before translating; its error wraps `KindInvalidRequest`. `Request.Extensions` is an `Extension` with `Provider() string` — type-assert your own and reject another provider's.

Gotcha recorded in project/gotchas.md: a second `json.WithUnmarshalers` in a `JoinOptions` **replaces** the first. Join the funcs (`json.JoinUnmarshalers`), not the options, or the second interface dispatch silently never fires.

Plan corrected in place (block quote under "Streams and events", plus a parenthetical in "The loop").

Handoff from the first build session (2026-09-14). All eight Foundation leaves are done and on main (through the stream leaf); the chat markdown renderer is also done. The next frontier is wave three: Anthropic wire (pIwqn0), OpenRouter wire (OEbtSj) and loop core (n1qE9c), which are disjoint by file and can fan out to three Opus agents from a clean main. After them: ant-stream, or-stream, hooks; then ant-live, or-live, loop-caps, chat-service.

What worked: one agent per leaf in its own worktree, Opus for anything with judgement, Sonnet only for the SSE framer; every brief restated the decided shapes and demanded "what in this brief is wrong" — that section produced the real findings (json/v2 required members, [N]byte, the Thinking name collision, the synctest context trap, the block-quote stack overflow). Integrate by snapshot commit on the branch, git merge --squash, read the whole staged diff, commit with -F, job done, remove the worktree.

Rulings the next briefs must carry (all also in the plan's block quotes and the leaf notes):
- Collect returns *Response; Complete returns *Response. Result carries the last Response, the Conversation, totals and Pending.
- Blocks is the named list type; Message.Content and ToolResult.Content are Blocks.
- ThinkingConfig is the request config; Thinking is the block. UnknownEvent is the event; Unknown is the block.
- Thinking.Raw is set by the provider at BlockStop only when the neutral fields cannot rebuild the wire block (OpenRouter reasoning_details); Anthropic rebuilds from Text and Signature and leaves Raw empty.
- OpenRouter must synthesise MessageStart, assign block indexes, emit BlockStart/BlockStop around runs, emit the trailing usage frame as a second MessageDelta and MessageStop once at [DONE]. native_finish_reason has no slot yet: rule on it in the or-wire brief (a Response field or an extension).
- Transport: providers inject an ErrorDecoder; the decoder is authoritative, the transport fills blanks; a decoder returning a non-retryable Kind for a 429 makes it terminal.
- Execute checks required parameters itself (json/v2 does not); the loop assigns ToolUseID and converts a handler error into an IsError result.
- Budget (MaxTurns default 20, MaxTokens, Timeout) lives in the loop leaf's budget.go.

Traps that cost time this session: never pipe a gating test run (one red build was committed that way, fixed next commit); agents sometimes leave their claim held, so job done may need job release <id> --as <name> first; two agents appending to gotchas.md conflict on squash-merge (keep both); json.JoinOptions with two WithUnmarshalers keeps only the last (gotchas).

Rulings for the dispatch (2026-09-15, integrator). Files owned: anthropic/wire.go, anthropic/translate.go, anthropic/thinking.go, anthropic/options.go (if needed) and tests. Nothing in the root package or openrouter/.
- Thinking: adaptive models get thinking{type:adaptive, display} + output_config.effort; budget-only models (Haiku 4.5 and older) get thinking{type:enabled, budget_tokens} derived from effort by a documented ratio of max_tokens; EffortOff is omitted on models that reject disabled (Fable 5.x). Which class a model is in comes from a single documented name heuristic in thinking.go with a table test; ModelInfo may override it later.
- Cache: Auto = top-level cache_control ephemeral plus one explicit marker on the last system block; Manual = the caller's markers, more than four is an error before sending; Off = none. TTL maps to cache_control.ttl.
- Thinking blocks are rebuilt from Text and Signature (Raw ignored); redacted from Data; Unknown blocks re-emit Raw verbatim.
- Usage: cache_creation_input_tokens -> CacheWrite, cache_read_input_tokens -> CacheRead. Cost is never reported. NativeStopReason stays empty: Anthropic's wire string is the StopReason.
- Extensions: an anthropic.Extensions struct implementing goodall.Extension with Provider() == "anthropic", carrying typed Beta constants and any other per-request Anthropic-only field; translation rejects a foreign Extension with KindInvalidRequest.

Rulings for the dispatch (2026-09-15, integrator). Files owned: openrouter/wire.go, openrouter/dialect.go, openrouter/translate.go and tests. Nothing in the root package or anthropic/.
- native_finish_reason now has a slot: MessageDelta.NativeStopReason and Response.NativeStopReason (commit 6e5731a). finish_reason maps stop->end_turn, length->max_tokens, tool_calls->tool_use, content_filter->refusal, unknown->StopReason(raw).
- Usage: Input = prompt_tokens minus cached and cache-write tokens so TotalInput() equals prompt_tokens; CacheRead = cached_tokens; CacheWrite = cache_write_tokens; Reasoning = reasoning_tokens. usage.cost decodes straight into Decimal (no float), Currency USD, Reported true. This translation lives here; the stream leaf calls it.
- Thinking blocks re-emit Raw (one reasoning_details entry per block) verbatim and in order; a block with no Raw is rebuilt as reasoning.text from Text and Signature.
- Dialect is a typed constant whose quirk table is a typed struct; Generic sends no OpenRouter-only field, asserted on bytes.
- Extensions: an openrouter.Extensions struct implementing goodall.Extension with Provider() == "openrouter": provider routing, models fallback, plugins, session id, debug echo. Attribution (referer, title) is a client option; define the type here, the client leaf sends the headers.

Rulings for the dispatch (2026-09-15, integrator). Files owned: agent.go, run.go, budget.go, stop.go, internal/fake/*.go and root tests in package goodall_test. Do not touch anthropic/ or openrouter/. Hooks (hooks.go, resume.go) are the next leaf: leave the Agent without a Hooks field; the hooks leaf adds it.
- The fake provider is a package, internal/fake, so the chat leaf can script runs too; loop tests are external tests (goodall_test) because internal/fake imports goodall.
- On a partial turn (cancellation or a stream error), the partial assistant message is appended with Partial set, and any complete tool_use block in it gets an IsError tool_result in the same unit so invariant 9 holds; tools already running are awaited and their real results used.
- Stop table: tool_use runs tools; pause_turn appends the message and resends; end_turn and stop_sequence are Done; max_tokens is Stopped MaxTokens with the tool calls not run; refusal is Stopped Refusal with the tool calls not run; anything else is Stopped UnknownStop. The table lives in stop.go with a test covering every row.
- Budget: MaxTurns zero means 20 and there is no unlimited mode; MaxTokens is the run's total usage; Timeout is wall clock via context.WithTimeoutCause so it is distinguishable from the caller's cancellation.
- Agent gains MaxTokens (per-turn output cap, zero for the provider's default); Logger is nil-safe.
